Commentary.Commentary: A brave effort by the Zimbabweans but it was not enough to win them their first T20I series. The second string Indian side pull through once again to emerge victorious. Zimbabwe have got plenty of cricket coming their way in the next few months at home while India travel to the West Indies for a 4-Test series in July. Do join us then. Goodbye and take care!

Triumphant Indian captain, MS DHONI says that games in this format often get close towards the end. He praises Zimbabwe for playing well and for making it a close series. He says that it was a very close game, but Zimbabwe need to play more matches and become more experienced as a team. He is disappointed that he didn't get a chance to bat in the ODI series but is happy with the outcome. He is happy with the progress in the bowling department and says that the fast bowling needs a good pool of players. He says all the bowlers did well in the series and that India now has some good bowlers for Tests, and eventually will have for the shorter formats of the game. He believes that close games like these help the team improve more than others and that the T20Is applied more pressure and were more beneficial than the ODI series.

Zimbabwean skipper, GRAEME CREMER says that he is happy with the way his players fought and credits India with a great performance. He is glad that his side came back well in the first T20I match and by how close they came to winning the series. He looks forward to playing a few more games in the future, including some Test matches, and looks forward to his team getting better.
Man of the Series, BARINDER SRAN says that he was confident that he could defend the 20 runs needed off the last over. Not everything went according to plan so he was forced to change it up a bit.
KEDAR JADHAV has been named the Man of the Match for his brilliant 58 off 42 balls.

Earlier in the day, Kedar Jadhav's brilliant 58 took India to 138 which looked moderate at the innings break but turned out to be more than enough in the end. Also, the last over of the Indian innings yielded 16 which proved to be very costly.

The Indian bowlers made the most of the variable bounce on the pitch, keeping the batsmen guessing and restricting them. Kulkarni got the valuable wicket of Sibanda while Axar removed Masakadza. Chahal was by far the most expensive of the lot, giving 32 runs in his four overs. Sran and Kulkarni picked up two wickets each but the former nearly gave it away in that final over.

The middle order batsmen Moor, Waller and Chigumbura, each tried to hold down the fort but were not successful as the pressure of the run chase bore down upon them. They needed 21 of the final over, but Maruma and Chigumbura made a fist of it, aided by a nervous Sran, as they nearly snatched victory from the jaws of defeat.

The hosts got off to a quick start, spurred on by the chanting of the crowd. Sibanda and Masakadza set up a 40-run partnership for the second wicket, raking in the runs in spurts. There was a brief period when Zimbabwe looked to be on the warpath and victory didn't seem like such a distant possibility. However, with the dismissals of Masakadza and Sibanda, the bowlers managed to get back into the game.
A very narrow win for India! In a nail-biting finish, the visitors clinch the T20I series 2-1! Zimbabwe will be gutted, they nearly had it in the bag but in the end India were the better side.

OUT! INDIA WIN! A tame finish to the game. Chigumbura comes down the track, takes it on the full and looks to go over the top but mistimes it to cover where the catch is taken with ease by Chahal. INDIA WIN BY 3 RUNS and TAKE THE 3-MATCH T2OI SERIES 2-1.
